statement: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{1+x}$ for $x>-1$. Find the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$ and show that $f(f(x))=\dfrac{x}{1+2x}$ for $x>0$.
solution: To invert, solve $y=\dfrac{x}{1+x}$ for $x$: $y(1+x)=x\Rightarrow x(1-y)=y\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{y}{1-y}$, so $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{x}{1-x}$ (domain $0<x<1$). For the composition, $f(f(x))=\dfrac{\frac{x}{1+x}}{1+\frac{x}{1+x}}=\dfrac{x}{1+2x}$ for $x>0$.
